import pandas as pd

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/training_1.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Source0 schema: ['business_id', 'Score', 'date', 'type']
# Source1 schema: ['business_id', 'date', 'ViolationTypeID', 'risk_category', 'description']

# Target schema: ['business_id': int, 'Score': float, 'date': int, 'type': str, 'ViolationTypeID': int, 'risk_category': str, 'description': str]

# Transformation plan:
# - Both sources share 'business_id' and 'date' columns.
# - Source0 has Score and type.
# - Source1 has ViolationTypeID, risk_category, description.
# - Join Source0 and Source1 on ['business_id', 'date'] to get all target columns.
# - The join is an inner join because target examples show all columns present.
# - Ensure data types match target schema.
# - Export the joined dataframe to the target CSV path.

# Perform inner join on ['business_id', 'date']
df_merged = pd.merge(df0, df1, on=['business_id', 'date'], how='inner')

# Enforce target schema data types
df_merged['business_id'] = df_merged['business_id'].astype(int)
df_merged['Score'] = df_merged['Score'].astype(float)
df_merged['date'] = df_merged['date'].astype(int)
df_merged['type'] = df_merged['type'].astype(str)
df_merged['ViolationTypeID'] = df_merged['ViolationTypeID'].astype(int)
df_merged['risk_category'] = df_merged['risk_category'].astype(str)
df_merged['description'] = df_merged['description'].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = ['business_id', 'Score', 'date', 'type', 'ViolationTypeID', 'risk_category', 'description']
df_target = df_merged[target_columns]

# Write the result to the specified target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on business_id and date (both integer columns, leftmost columns in target schema)
# Use inner join to keep only matching rows (to avoid losing rows or adding extra rows)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', on=['business_id', 'date'])

# Write output with exact target schema and column order
joined = joined[['business_id', 'Score', 'date', 'type', 'ViolationTypeID', 'risk_category', 'description']]

joined.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_37/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
